position: before its word — *terrifically talented*; end in the manner sense

senses.gloss: Extremely; very — usually in a good sense.
examples: She's *terrifically* talented and very modest about it.
The new restaurant has been doing *terrifically* well.
It was a *terrifically* exciting game.

position: end
modifies: verbs, especially verbs of speaking and writing

senses.gloss: In a brief, unfriendly way, using very few words.
examples: "No comment," the senator said *tersely*.
She replied *tersely* to my long email.
The company issued a *tersely* worded statement.

position: end

senses.gloss: In an irritated, impatient way.
examples: "I heard you the first time," he said *testily*.
The coach answered reporters' questions *testily* after the loss.
She tapped her pen *testily* on the desk.

position: end — in the manner sense; front with a comma in the viewpoint sense
comparison: more/most — in the manner sense; not gradable in the viewpoint sense
modifies: verbs; clauses in the viewpoint sense

senses.gloss: In an exaggerated way that is meant to attract attention.
examples: He sighed *theatrically* and rolled his eyes.
She clutched her chest *theatrically* when she saw the bill.
The villain laughed *theatrically* as he left the stage.

senses.gloss: In terms of the theater or of staging a play.
examples: *Theatrically*, the production is a triumph.
The script is strong, but *theatrically* it doesn't quite work.

position: before its word — *thematically linked*; also front with a comma or end

senses.gloss: In terms of themes or subjects.
examples: The three novels are *thematically* linked.
*Thematically*, the album deals with loss and recovery.
The exhibit is organized *thematically* rather than by date.

position: before its word — *theologically conservative*; also front with a comma

senses.gloss: In terms of religious belief and theology.
examples: The church is *theologically* conservative.
*Theologically*, the two groups have little in common.
Her argument is *theologically* sound.

position: end — also before an adjective (*therapeutically effective*)

senses.gloss: In a way that treats an illness or helps a person heal.
examples: The drug is used *therapeutically* for chronic pain.
A dose can be *therapeutically* effective and still cause side effects.
Many people find that gardening works *therapeutically* for stress.

position: end — almost always after *or*: *in 1990 or thereabouts*
modifies: a number, time or place just mentioned

senses.gloss: Approximately — near the number, amount or time just mentioned.
examples: The house was built in 1920 or *thereabouts*.
The repair will cost $500 or *thereabouts*.

senses.gloss: Near the place just mentioned.
examples: They live in Tulsa or somewhere *thereabouts*.
The accident happened on Route 9 or *thereabouts*.

position: end — also front, and after *shortly* or *soon* (*shortly thereafter*)

senses.gloss: After that time; from then on.
examples: He retired in 2010 and died shortly *thereafter*.
The first payment is due in May, with monthly payments *thereafter*.
*Thereafter*, the town grew quickly.

position: mid — usually before an *-ing* form (*thereby reducing…*)
modifies: clauses — gives the result of the action just described

senses.gloss: As a result of that action.
examples: The company cut prices, *thereby* attracting new customers.
By signing the contract, she *thereby* accepted its terms.
Exercise lowers blood pressure, *thereby* reducing the risk of stroke.

type: place — in that thing or matter
position: end — front only in *therein lies…*

senses.gloss: In that place, document or matter.
examples: *Therein* lies the problem.
Read the contract and the terms contained *therein*.
The school's rules, and the penalties described *therein*, apply to every student.

type: linking — refers back to something just mentioned (*of it*, *of that*)
position: after its word — *or lack thereof*
form: *there* + *of* — formal and legal; everyday English uses it mostly in *or lack thereof*

senses.gloss: Of it or of that — referring to something just mentioned.
examples: He was judged on his experience, or lack *thereof*.
The landlord may keep the deposit or any part *thereof*.
She pointed out the evidence, or rather the absence *thereof*.

position: before its word — *thermally insulated*; also end

senses.gloss: In terms of heat, or by means of heat.
examples: The new windows are *thermally* efficient.
The pipes are *thermally* insulated to keep them from freezing.
The metal parts expand *thermally* as the engine warms up.

position: end — after the verb or its object
form: flat — the same form as the adjective *thick*
contrast: The flat adverb is informal and mostly fixed: *spread it thick*, *thick and fast*, *lay it on thick* (to exaggerate or flatter too much). In careful writing use *thickly*. In *a thick book*, *thick* is an adjective.

senses.gloss: In a thick layer, or densely.
examples: Spread the frosting on *thick*.
Complaints came in *thick* and fast after the price increase.
Cut the bread a little *thicker* for toast.

position: end — also before a participle (*thickly wooded*)

senses.gloss: In a thick layer, or close together in large numbers.
examples: Butter the bread *thickly*.
The hills are *thickly* wooded.
Snow lay *thickly* on the roofs.

senses.gloss: In a low, unclear voice, because of emotion, illness or drink.
examples: "I'm sorry," he said *thickly*, fighting back tears.
She spoke *thickly* through her cold.

position: end — after the verb or its object
form: flat — the same form as the adjective *thin*
contrast: The flat adverb is informal and mostly fixed: *slice it thin*, *spread yourself too thin*. In careful writing use *thinly*. In *a thin book*, *thin* is an adjective.

senses.gloss: In thin slices or a thin layer.
examples: Slice the onions *thin*.
Roll the dough a little *thinner* this time.
You're spreading yourself too *thin* with three jobs.

position: end — after the verb (*slice it thinly*); before its word in the degree sense (*thinly populated*)

senses.gloss: In thin slices or a thin layer.
examples: Slice the cucumber *thinly*.
Apply the paint *thinly* and let it dry.

senses.gloss: With only a little of something — few people, little cover, or little effort to hide.
examples: The area is *thinly* populated.
It was a *thinly* veiled threat.
The meeting was *thinly* attended.

position: front or end — *Third, …*; *came in third*
form: the ordinal *third* used as an adverb — also *thirdly*

senses.gloss: In the third place in a list of points.
examples: *Third*, the plan costs too much.
First, it's cheap; second, it's fast; and *third*, it's safe.

senses.gloss: In third position in a race, contest or ranking.
examples: She finished *third* in the marathon.
Our team came in *third* this year.

type: linking — introduces the third point in a list
position: front — at the start of the sentence, usually with a comma
contrast: American writers often prefer *third* to *thirdly*; both are correct, but keep the series consistent: *first*, *second*, *third* or *firstly*, *secondly*, *thirdly*.

senses.gloss: Used to introduce the third point in a list.
examples: *Thirdly*, we need more volunteers.
Firstly, it's too expensive; secondly, it's too slow; and *thirdly*, nobody asked for it.
*Thirdly*, the report ignores the cost of maintenance.

position: end

senses.gloss: In a way that shows you are very thirsty or eager for something.
examples: The dog lapped *thirstily* at the bowl.
He drank the cold water *thirstily*.
The dry soil soaked up the rain *thirstily*.

position: end — also mid, and before a participle (*thoughtfully designed*)

senses.gloss: In a quiet, serious way, while thinking.
examples: She looked at him *thoughtfully* before answering.
He rubbed his chin *thoughtfully*.

senses.gloss: In a kind or careful way that shows you have thought about other people's needs.
examples: The hotel had *thoughtfully* left a map in our room.
The house is *thoughtfully* designed for wheelchair users.

position: mid or end

senses.gloss: Without thinking about the results or about other people.
examples: He *thoughtlessly* parked in front of our driveway.
She spoke *thoughtlessly* and hurt her friend's feelings.
People toss trash *thoughtlessly* out of their car windows.

position: end

senses.gloss: In a way that suggests harm or danger.
examples: The dog growled *threateningly*.
He stepped *threateningly* toward me.
Dark clouds gathered *threateningly* over the hills.

position: end — after a verb of change (*grew threefold*)

senses.gloss: Three times as much or as many.
examples: Sales have increased *threefold* since 2019.
The price of eggs rose almost *threefold* in a year.
For smokers, the risk grows *threefold*.

position: end

senses.gloss: Carefully, without wasting money.
examples: They lived *thriftily* and saved for retirement.
She shops *thriftily*, always checking the sale racks first.
The apartment was *thriftily* furnished with secondhand pieces.

position: end
contrast: Most often a preposition (*throughout the country*, *throughout the year*). It is an adverb only when no noun follows (*painted white throughout*).

senses.gloss: In every part of a place or thing.
examples: The house has been painted white *throughout*.
The hotel offers free Wi-Fi *throughout*.

senses.gloss: During the whole time of an event.
senses.ru: всё время, с начала до конца
examples: The movie was sad, but the kids laughed *throughout*.
He stayed calm *throughout*.

position: end
contrast: Many editors call *thusly* nonstandard or jokey, because *thus* is already an adverb. In careful writing use *thus* or *like this*.

senses.gloss: In this way; like this — informal and often humorous.
examples: The steps should be written *thusly*: ingredients first, then directions.
He explained his theory *thusly*.
Fold the napkin *thusly*, and it will look like a swan.

position: end — also before a participle (*tidily folded*)

senses.gloss: In a neat and orderly way.
examples: Her sweaters were *tidily* folded in the drawer.
Please stack the chairs *tidily* against the wall.
The story wraps up a little too *tidily* at the end.

position: end — also before a participle (*tightly packed*)
contrast: *tight* is also an adverb, but only in informal set phrases (*hold tight*, *sleep tight*, *shut tight*). *tightly* works everywhere and is the only choice before a participle (*tightly packed*, not *tight packed*).

senses.gloss: Firmly and securely, so that something does not move or open.
examples: She held her son's hand *tightly*.
Make sure the lid is *tightly* closed.
He shut his eyes *tightly*.

senses.gloss: Closely, with little space or freedom.
examples: The crowd was *tightly* packed into the square.
Access to the building is *tightly* controlled.

position: end — also mid

senses.gloss: In a shy, nervous way, without confidence.
examples: The girl *timidly* raised her hand.
He knocked *timidly* on the office door.
"Can I come in?" she asked *timidly*.

position: end

senses.gloss: In a way that shows you are tired.
examples: She smiled *tiredly* and sat down.
He rubbed his eyes *tiredly*.
"Let's talk about it tomorrow," he said *tiredly*.

position: mid or end

senses.gloss: With great effort, for a long time, without stopping.
examples: She worked *tirelessly* to raise money for the shelter.
Firefighters worked *tirelessly* through the night.
He has *tirelessly* campaigned for cleaner air.

position: before its word — *tiresomely long*; end after a verb

senses.gloss: In a boring or annoying way.
examples: The speech was *tiresomely* long.
He talked *tiresomely* about his golf game.
The jokes soon became *tiresomely* familiar.

position: end — mostly in *go toe-to-toe with*
form: *toe* + *to* + *toe* — from boxing; also an adjective (*a toe-to-toe battle*)

senses.gloss: In a direct, close fight or contest, as equals.
examples: The small company went *toe-to-toe* with the tech giants.
The two candidates stood *toe-to-toe* in the final debate.
The boxers fought *toe-to-toe* for twelve rounds.

position: before its word — *tolerably well*

senses.gloss: Fairly; well enough, but not very.
examples: He speaks Spanish *tolerably* well.
The motel was *tolerably* clean.
The weather stayed *tolerably* warm all week.

position: end

senses.gloss: In a patient way that accepts other people's views, habits or faults.
examples: She smiled *tolerantly* at the children's noise.
He listened *tolerantly* to his father's old stories.
Good teachers treat students' mistakes *tolerantly*.

position: end

senses.gloss: In a flat voice that shows no feeling.
examples: "He's gone," she said *tonelessly*.
The officer read out the charges *tonelessly*.
He answered every question *tonelessly*, staring at the floor.

position: end — also between commas
form: idiom — also an adjective (*a tongue-in-cheek review*)

senses.gloss: Not seriously; jokingly, while seeming to be serious.
examples: He suggested, *tongue-in-cheek*, that we cancel Mondays.
The article was clearly written *tongue-in-cheek*.
She said it *tongue-in-cheek*, but some people took her seriously.

position: end

senses.gloss: On the surface of the body rather than by mouth or injection — a medical use.
examples: The cream should be applied *topically* twice a day.
The drug is used *topically* to treat acne.
Some antibiotics work better *topically* than in pill form.

position: end — mostly after *turn* or *go*
form: rhyming compound — also an adjective (*a topsy-turvy world*)

senses.gloss: Upside down, or into a state of confusion.
examples: The storm turned the whole campground *topsy-turvy*.
The news turned all our plans *topsy-turvy*.
Everything went *topsy-turvy* when the twins were born.

position: end — after a verb of movement; before its word in the degree sense (*tortuously complicated*)
modifies: verbs; adjectives in the degree sense
contrast: Do not confuse it with *torturously* (painfully, like torture). *tortuously* is about twists and complications: *a tortuously slow process* is slow because it is complicated, while *torturously slow* means painfully slow. Even native writers mix them up.

senses.gloss: In a winding, twisting way.
examples: The road winds *tortuously* up the mountain.
The river twists *tortuously* through the valley.

senses.gloss: In a long, overly complicated way.
examples: The contract is *tortuously* complicated.
The bill moved *tortuously* through Congress for two years.

position: before its word — *torturously slow*
contrast: Do not confuse it with *tortuously* (in a winding or overly complicated way). *torturously* comes from *torture*; *tortuously* comes from *tortuous*, twisting.

senses.gloss: In a way that causes great pain or suffering; painfully.
examples: The last hour of the flight passed *torturously* slowly.
The climb to the summit was *torturously* steep.
The wait for the test results was *torturously* long.

position: before its word — *touchingly naive*; end after a verb

senses.gloss: In a way that makes you feel sympathy or tenderness.
examples: The film is *touchingly* honest about grief.
He was *touchingly* proud of his daughter.
She spoke *touchingly* about her late husband.

position: any position — front with a comma; mid (*has traditionally voted*); before a participle (*traditionally served*)

senses.gloss: According to custom, or to what has usually been done for a long time.
examples: *Traditionally*, the bride's family pays for the wedding.
Turkey is *traditionally* served at Thanksgiving.
The state has *traditionally* voted Republican.

position: any position — mid or end in the manner sense; front with a comma as a comment (*Tragically, …*)

senses.gloss: In a very sad way, especially one involving death or suffering.
examples: He died *tragically* young.
The trip ended *tragically* when their boat sank.

senses.gloss: Used to say that a fact is very sad.
senses.ru: к несчастью, как это ни трагично
examples: *Tragically*, none of the passengers survived.
*Tragically*, the warning came too late.

position: end

senses.gloss: In a calm, peaceful way.
examples: The baby slept *tranquilly* in her crib.
The lake lay *tranquilly* under the morning mist.
Cows grazed *tranquilly* in the field.

position: end — usually after *used*
contrast: The opposite is *intransitively*: *run* is used transitively in *run a business* and intransitively in *run fast*.

senses.gloss: As a transitive verb — with a direct object.
examples: *Grow* can be used *transitively*, as in *grow tomatoes*.
In this sentence the verb *break* is used *transitively*.
Some verbs can be used both *transitively* and intransitively.

position: end — in the manner sense; before its word in the degree sense (*transparently false*)
modifies: verbs; adjectives in the degree sense

senses.gloss: Openly, so that people can see what is being done.
examples: The city must spend public money *transparently*.
The charity operates *transparently* and publishes its accounts online.

senses.gloss: Very obviously — about a lie or a motive that is easy to see through.
examples: His excuse was *transparently* false.
It was a *transparently* political move.

position: before its word — *treacherously icy*; mid or end in the betrayal sense
modifies: adjectives; verbs in the betrayal sense

senses.gloss: In a way that is dangerous, often more than it looks.
examples: The roads were *treacherously* icy this morning.
The rocks near the shore are *treacherously* slippery.

senses.gloss: By betraying someone who trusted you.
examples: He *treacherously* sold the plans to a rival company.
The general was *treacherously* murdered by his own officers.

position: end
modifies: verbs, especially of speaking and smiling

senses.gloss: In a shaky way, because of fear, nervousness or strong emotion.
examples: "Is anyone there?" she asked *tremulously*.
He smiled *tremulously* through his tears.
Her voice rose *tremulously* on the last note.

position: end — also mid, and before a participle (*trenchantly argued*)
modifies: verbs of speaking and writing, and participles

senses.gloss: In a sharp, clear and forceful way — about criticism or argument.
examples: She *trenchantly* criticized the new policy.
The essay is *trenchantly* argued.
He wrote *trenchantly* about corruption in city politics.

position: end — also mid

senses.gloss: In a way that shows pride and joy at winning or succeeding.
examples: She waved the winning ticket *triumphantly*.
The team returned home *triumphantly* to a hero's welcome.
"I told you so," he said *triumphantly*.

position: before its word — *trivially easy*; end after a verb

senses.gloss: So simply or so slightly that it hardly matters or needs explaining.
examples: The fix was *trivially* easy once we found the bug.
The statement is *trivially* true.
The two versions differ only *trivially*.

position: end — also mid

senses.gloss: In a way that shows you believe someone is honest or will not hurt you.
examples: The child looked up at her *trustingly*.
The puppy followed him *trustingly* down the street.
She *trustingly* gave the caller her bank details.

position: end — in the manner sense; front with a comma as a stance adverb
comparison: more/most — in the manner sense (*more truthfully*); not gradable as a stance adverb
modifies: verbs; clauses as a stance adverb

senses.gloss: Honestly; without lying.
examples: Please answer the questions *truthfully*.
He could *truthfully* say he had never cheated.

senses.gloss: Used to show that you are giving your honest opinion.
examples: *Truthfully*, I never liked that job.
*Truthfully*, I have no idea what happened.

position: end

senses.gloss: Without a clear or pleasant tune.
examples: He whistled *tunelessly* while he worked.
She hummed *tunelessly* to herself.
The kids sang *tunelessly* but happily.

position: end — after a verb of change (*rose twofold*)
form: *two* + *-fold* — more often an adjective (*a twofold purpose*)

senses.gloss: Twice as much or as many.
examples: The number of applicants increased *twofold*.
Rents have risen nearly *twofold* in five years.
The risk of injury rose *twofold* among older players.

position: mid — also front with a comma; before its word in the 'characteristically' sense
modifies: verbs and clauses; adjectives in the 'characteristically' sense

senses.gloss: Usually; in most cases.
examples: The trip *typically* takes about three hours.
*Typically*, the store closes at nine.

senses.gloss: In a way that is characteristic of a person, group or thing.
examples: It was a *typically* American breakfast of eggs and bacon.
He was *typically* modest about his success.

type: time — in the end; also stance (*basically*)
position: mid — also front with a comma
contrast: A false friend: it does not mean 'in the form of an ultimatum' (ультимативно). It means 'in the end' or 'at the most basic level'.

senses.gloss: In the end, after a long process; or at the most basic level.
examples: The project *ultimately* cost twice as much as planned.
Their marriage *ultimately* ended in divorce.
*Ultimately*, the decision is yours.

position: before its word — *unabashedly romantic*; also mid

senses.gloss: Openly, without embarrassment or apology.
examples: The film is *unabashedly* sentimental.
She is *unabashedly* proud of her hometown.
He *unabashedly* admitted he had never read the book.

position: before its word — *unacceptably high*; end after a verb

senses.gloss: To a degree or in a way that cannot be accepted.
examples: Unemployment remains *unacceptably* high.
The wait times at the clinic are *unacceptably* long.
He behaved *unacceptably* at the meeting.

position: before its word — *unaccountably nervous*; also mid, or front with a comma

senses.gloss: In a way that nobody can explain; for some unknown reason.
examples: She felt *unaccountably* sad all day.
The letter was *unaccountably* delayed.
*Unaccountably*, the key was back in the drawer.

position: before its word — *unalterably opposed*; also mid

senses.gloss: In a way that cannot be changed.
examples: The senator is *unalterably* opposed to the tax increase.
The accident *unalterably* changed his life.
Their friendship was *unalterably* damaged by the lawsuit.

position: end — also mid

senses.gloss: Clearly, in a way that can only be understood one way.
examples: The law states *unambiguously* that the tax applies to everyone.
The results *unambiguously* support the theory.
Voters rejected the plan *unambiguously*.

position: end — also mid

senses.gloss: With everyone agreeing or voting the same way.
examples: The board voted *unanimously* to approve the budget.
The bill passed the Senate *unanimously*.
Critics *unanimously* praised her performance.

position: mid — also front with a comma, and before an adjective

senses.gloss: Used to say that something is true and nobody could disagree.
examples: She is *unarguably* the best player on the team.
*Unarguably*, the city needs more affordable housing.
It was *unarguably* a mistake.

position: before its word — *unashamedly romantic*; also mid

senses.gloss: Openly, without feeling ashamed or embarrassed.
examples: The novel is *unashamedly* romantic.
He cried *unashamedly* at his daughter's wedding.
The show is *unashamedly* old-fashioned.

position: before its word — *unattractively designed*; also end

senses.gloss: In a way that is not pleasant to look at or not appealing.
examples: The food was *unattractively* served on paper plates.
The old mall is *unattractively* designed, with no windows at all.
He was *unattractively* smug about his win.

ru: неизбежно, по не зависящим от нас причинам
position: mid — also before a participle (*unavoidably delayed*)

senses.gloss: In a way that cannot be prevented.
examples: The flight was *unavoidably* delayed by the storm.
The doctor was *unavoidably* detained at the hospital.
On a project this large, some mistakes will *unavoidably* happen.

position: end — mostly in *catch* or *take someone unawares*
contrast: Do not confuse it with the adjective *unaware* (*I was unaware of the problem*). *unawares* is the adverb (*The news caught me unawares*).

senses.gloss: By surprise, when someone is not ready or expecting it.
examples: The early snowstorm caught the city *unawares*.
The question took her *unawares*, and she didn't know what to say.
The guards were caught *unawares* by the attack.

position: before its word — *unbearably hot*

senses.gloss: To a degree that is too unpleasant or painful to accept.
examples: It was *unbearably* hot in the car.
The music next door was *unbearably* loud.
The waiting was *unbearably* painful.

type: manner — always with *to*: without someone's knowledge
position: front — *unbeknownst to me, …*; also between commas
form: *un-* + old *beknown* (known) + *-st*; *unbeknown* is a rarer, mostly British variant

senses.gloss: Without someone knowing about it — always followed by *to*.
examples: *Unbeknownst* to her parents, she had dropped out of college.
*Unbeknownst* to us, the tickets had already sold out.
The company had, *unbeknownst* to its customers, been selling their data.

position: before its word — *unbelievably good*; front with a comma as a comment
modifies: adjectives and adverbs; clauses as a comment

senses.gloss: Extremely — to a degree that is hard to believe.
examples: The view from the top was *unbelievably* beautiful.
He's *unbelievably* rude to waiters.

senses.gloss: Used to say that something is surprising and hard to believe.
examples: *Unbelievably*, nobody was hurt in the crash.
*Unbelievably*, the store was still open at midnight.

position: end
contrast: Do not confuse it with *unbelievably* (extremely; surprisingly). *She stared unbelievingly* describes how she looked; *She was unbelievably tired* means very tired.

senses.gloss: In a way that shows you cannot believe what you see or hear.
examples: She stared *unbelievingly* at the lottery ticket.
He shook his head *unbelievingly* when he heard the score.
"You did what?" his mother asked *unbelievingly*.

position: end

senses.gloss: Without blinking; steadily, without looking away or showing emotion.
examples: The cat stared at me *unblinkingly*.
She looked *unblinkingly* at the judge.
The documentary looks *unblinkingly* at life in prison.

position: before its word — *uncannily accurate*

senses.gloss: In a strange, surprising way that is hard to explain.
examples: She looks *uncannily* like her grandmother.
His prediction turned out to be *uncannily* accurate.
The house was *uncannily* quiet.

position: mid or end

senses.gloss: Without stopping; continuously.
examples: The rain fell *unceasingly* for three days.
She worked *unceasingly* to find a cure.
The neighbor's dog barked *unceasingly* all night.

position: end — also mid, and before a participle (*unceremoniously dumped*)

senses.gloss: Suddenly and rudely, without politeness or any ceremony.
examples: He was *unceremoniously* fired after twenty years with the company.
The bouncer threw them *unceremoniously* out of the club.
Her old sofa was *unceremoniously* dumped on the curb.

position: end — also mid

senses.gloss: In a way that shows doubt or a lack of confidence.
examples: She smiled *uncertainly* at the stranger.
He stood *uncertainly* in the doorway.
The toddler walked *uncertainly* across the room.

position: before its word — *uncharacteristically quiet*; also front with a comma

senses.gloss: In a way that is not typical of someone or something.
examples: He was *uncharacteristically* quiet at dinner.
The team played *uncharacteristically* badly.
*Uncharacteristically*, she forgot my birthday.

position: end — also before a participle (*unclearly written*)

senses.gloss: In a way that is hard to understand, see or hear.
examples: The instructions were *unclearly* written.
He spoke so *unclearly* that nobody understood him.
If you express yourself *unclearly*, people will guess what you mean.

position: end — in the manner sense; before its word in the degree sense (*uncomfortably hot*)
modifies: verbs; adjectives and adverbs in the degree sense

senses.gloss: In a way that shows you feel physically uncomfortable or embarrassed.
examples: He shifted *uncomfortably* in his chair.
She laughed *uncomfortably* at the joke.

senses.gloss: To an unpleasant or worrying degree.
examples: It was *uncomfortably* hot in the office.
The hurricane came *uncomfortably* close to the coast.

position: before its word — *uncommonly good*

senses.gloss: Unusually; to an unusual degree.
examples: She is an *uncommonly* gifted pianist.
It's *uncommonly* warm for February.
He was *uncommonly* kind to us.

position: mid or end

senses.gloss: Without complaining.
examples: She *uncomplainingly* cared for her sick mother for years.
The soldiers marched *uncomplainingly* through the rain.
He accepted the extra work *uncomplainingly*.

position: before its word — *uncompromisingly honest*; also end

senses.gloss: Without changing your ideas or standards to please anyone.
examples: The film is *uncompromisingly* bleak.
She is *uncompromisingly* honest with her students.
He fought *uncompromisingly* for workers' rights.

position: end

senses.gloss: In a calm way that shows you are not worried or not interested.
examples: He shrugged *unconcernedly* and went back to his book.
The cat watched *unconcernedly* as the dog barked at it.
She walked *unconcernedly* past the long line.

position: end

senses.gloss: Without any conditions or limits.
examples: Most parents love their children *unconditionally*.
The army surrendered *unconditionally*.
The prisoners were released *unconditionally*.

position: mid or end

senses.gloss: Without knowing it or intending it.
examples: She *unconsciously* touches her hair when she's nervous.
We often copy our parents' habits *unconsciously*.
He was *unconsciously* tapping his foot to the music.

position: end — also mid

senses.gloss: In a way that goes against a country's constitution.
examples: The court ruled that the police had acted *unconstitutionally*.
The law *unconstitutionally* limits free speech.
Critics say the governor spent the funds *unconstitutionally*.

position: end

senses.gloss: In a way that cannot be stopped or controlled.
examples: She laughed *uncontrollably* at his joke.
His hands were shaking *uncontrollably*.
The fire spread *uncontrollably* through the dry forest.

position: end — also before a participle

senses.gloss: In a way that is different from what most people do.
examples: She dresses *unconventionally* for a lawyer.
The house is *unconventionally* designed, with no interior walls.
He was raised *unconventionally* on a sailboat.

position: end

senses.gloss: In a way that does not make people believe you.
examples: "I'm fine," she said *unconvincingly*.
He argued *unconvincingly* that the money had been a gift.
The actor played the villain *unconvincingly*.

position: mid or end

senses.gloss: Without questioning whether something is true or good.
examples: Many people *uncritically* accept what they read online.
The reporter repeated the company's claims *uncritically*.
Fans praised the sequel *uncritically*.

position: end

senses.gloss: In a way that ignores people's right to vote or have a say.
examples: The leader was accused of ruling *undemocratically*.
The decision was made *undemocratically*, without a vote.
The party chose its candidate *undemocratically*.

position: mid — also front with a comma, and before an adjective

senses.gloss: Used to say that something is certainly true.
examples: She is *undeniably* talented.
*Undeniably*, the plan has some problems.
The new design is *undeniably* better than the old one.

position: end
modifies: verbs such as *go*, *stay*, *put*; numbers in *and under*
contrast: Most often a preposition (*under the table*). It is an adverb only when no noun follows (*The boat went under*). *go under* also means that a business fails.

senses.gloss: Below something, especially below the surface of water.
examples: The boat hit the rocks and went *under*.
She took a deep breath and stayed *under* for a full minute.

senses.gloss: Less than a stated number, amount or age.
examples: Tickets are $10 for kids 12 and *under*.
Anyone who scores 50 or *under* has to retake the test.

senses.gloss: Unconscious, especially because of an anesthetic.
examples: The patient was put *under* for the surgery.
He was *under* for about two hours.
